say.en: Your bill is the price of each item times how many you bought, all added up. Matrix multiplication does exactly this: row times column, then add. In this lesson: Decide when AB is defined and find its order.
Multiply matrices.
See that AB is not equal to BA in general.

body.en: If $A$ is $m \times n$ and $B$ is $n \times p$, then $AB$ is the $m \times p$ matrix with $(AB)_{ik} = \sum_{j} a_{ij} b_{jk}$: multiply row $i$ of $A$ with *column* $k$ of $B$ term by term and add. $AB$ is defined only when columns of $A$ = rows of $B$.
body.kn: A, m × n ಮತ್ತು B, n × p ಆದರೆ AB, m × p. A ಯ i ನೇ ಸಾಲನ್ನು B ಯ k ನೇ ಕಂಬಸಾಲಿನೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪದದಿಂದ ಪದಕ್ಕೆ ಗುಣಿಸಿ ಕೂಡಿಸಿ.

points.en: Inner orders must match: (m × n)(n × p) = m × p
Row of A into *column* of B

narration.en: To multiply, take a row of A and a column of B, multiply matching entries and add. The product exists only when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B.

say.en: Row of A into column of B.
A m by n matrix times an n by p matrix: the inner numbers must match, and the outer numbers give the order of the product.
Each entry is a row of A times a column of B: multiply term by term and add. Row 1 with column 1 gives 1 times 5 plus 2 times 7, that is 19.
Doing all four entries gives AB. Now swap the order: BA is a different matrix. Matrix multiplication is not commutative.
Even stranger: two non-zero matrices can multiply to give the zero matrix.

Matrix *multiplication* is associative, $(AB)C = A(BC)$, and distributive, $A(B + C) = AB + AC$; $AI = IA = A$. But it is not commutative: usually $AB 
e BA$. Also $AB = O$ is possible with $A 
e O$ and $B 
e O$.

steps.en: BA: row 1 of B picks row 2 of A, row 2 picks row 1: BA = [3 4; 1 2].

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A = [1 2; 3 4], B = [0 1; 1 0]. Find AB and BA.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A = [1 2; 3 4], B = [0 1; 1 0]. Find AB and BA.
AB: row 1 gives (1 0 plus 2 1, 1 1 plus 2 0) equals (2, 1); row 2 gives (4, 3).
BA: row 1 of B picks row 2 of A, row 2 picks row 1: BA = [3 4; 1 2].
So the answer is AB = [2 1; 4 3] is not equal to BA = [3 4; 1 2].

problem.en: Show that A = [3 1; −1 2] satisfies A² − 5A + 7I = O.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Show that A = [3 1; −1 2] satisfies A² − 5A + 7I = O.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Show that A = [3 1; minus 1 2] satisfies A squared minus 5A plus 7I equals O.
A squared = [9 minus 1, 3 plus 2; minus 3 minus 2, minus 1 plus 4] = [8 5; minus 5 3].
5A = [15 5; minus 5 10], so A squared minus 5A = [-7 0; 0 minus 7].
Adding 7I gives O.
So the answer is A squared minus 5A plus 7I equals O.
